title: Bhuvneshwar Kumar to Captain India at Hong Kong Sixes 2026
excerpt: The veteran pacer will lead an IPL-heavy Indian seven at the October 30–November 1 six-a-side tournament in Hong Kong, with Krunal Pandya, Rahul Tewatia and T. Natarajan among the squad.
body:
• Bhuvneshwar Kumar will captain India's seven-member squad at the Hong Kong Sixes 2026, played October 30 to November 1 at the Tin Kwong Road Recreation Ground.
  • The IPL-heavy squad includes Krunal Pandya, Shashank Singh, Rahul Tewatia, Nitish Rana, Rahul Tripathi and T. Natarajan; the tournament will be broadcast live in India on Sony Sports Network.
  • The six-a-side format demands every player contribute across disciplines in rapid-fire, high-scoring games; India returns looking to go deeper after bowing out following a two-run DLS win over Pakistan in 2025.
  • Pakistan enter as defending champions with a record sixth title; twelve teams — eight major nations and four associates — will take part, with JSW Sports on board as commercial partner.

A rare format, a familiar name at the helm

Bhuvneshwar Kumar has been named captain of Team India for the 2026 Hong Kong Sixes, the storied six-a-side cricket tournament that returns to Hong Kong from October 30 to November 1. The veteran seamer, a mainstay of India's white-ball sides through the 2010s and a two-time IPL champion with Royal Challengers Bengaluru in 2025 and 2026, will lead a seven-member Indian contingent composed almost entirely of IPL performers, according to a press release from the tournament organizers.

https://x.com/CricCrazyJohns/status/2107008631984291882

Alongside Bhuvneshwar will be his RCB teammate and fellow IPL champion Krunal Pandya, plus Shashank Singh (Punjab Kings), Rahul Tewatia (Gujarat Titans), Nitish Rana (Delhi Capitals), Rahul Tripathi (Kolkata Knight Riders) and T. Natarajan (Delhi Capitals). It is a squad built for entertainment value as much as results — explosive batting, proven finishing ability and specialist bowling compressed into cricket's fastest format.

A squad built for the format's demands

The Hong Kong Sixes is one of cricket's most distinctive competitions: six players a side, five-over games, and a format in which every player is required to bat, bowl and field in roles far beyond their usual brief. There is little room to settle in; matches are high-scoring, boundaries come thick and fast, and momentum shifts in the space of a single over.

That, the organizers say, is precisely why India's line-up is intriguing. Bhuvneshwar brings the new-ball intelligence that made him one of India's most dependable pacers, Krunal the all-round versatility, Rana the top-order aggression, Shashank and Tewatia the proven finishing punch that has swung IPL games, Tripathi the attacking intent and Natarajan the specialist left-arm pace option.

"We are very grateful to the Indian cricket authorities for their support in helping us put together arguably one of the strongest sides that has represented India in the history of the Sixes. This will surely prove to be a quantum leap forward in terms of viewership and further validation for this iconic tournament."— Anuraag Bhatnagar, Director of Marketing and Commercial, Cricket Hong Kong, China

Unfinished business from 2025

India return to the Sixes with something to prove. The 2025 campaign opened with a dramatic two-run DLS victory over Pakistan before ending in defeat in the subsequent matches and an early exit. This year's field will be formidable: Pakistan enter as defending champions, having beaten debutants Kuwait in last year's final to claim a record sixth Hong Kong Sixes title.

The 2026 edition will feature twelve teams — eight major cricketing nations alongside four associate members — and is the first to be run with JSW Sports as commercial partner. Tickets for all three days are on sale at HKD 780, and the tournament will air live in India on Sony Sports Network.

Why it matters for the diaspora

For cricket fans across the United States and Canada, the Sixes offers something the long-form calendar rarely does: India's stars in a condensed, prime-time-friendly spectacle where every ball matters. An IPL-heavy Indian squad playing a format built for highlight reels is tailor-made for the growing American audience discovering cricket on its own terms.

What's next

The action begins October 30 at the Tin Kwong Road Recreation Ground. Whether Bhuvneshwar's mix of seam intelligence and IPL finishing power can carry India past Pakistan and the rest of a strong field will be answered across three days of high-octane six-a-side cricket.
